ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached logo is bounded above by one large semicircular arc spanning the full width. At the bottom left there is a bulging semicircular part, and at the bottom right there is a semicircular cut-out. The shaded region is the lower-left part of the logo, and its boundary includes an S-shaped divider made from two smaller semicircular arcs. The diagram is marked not drawn to scale, so the given radii information is used rather than visual measurement. Reasoning: Since all arcs have radii 2 cm, 4 cm, or 8 cm, the full-width outer semicircle has radius 8, the two medium lower arcs have radius 4, and the two small S-divider arcs have radius 2. The area of a semicircle of radius r is (1/2)πr^2. The whole logo area is the large radius-8 semicircle plus the lower-left radius-4 semicircle minus the lower-right radius-4 semicircular cut-out. The two radius-4 terms cancel, so the whole logo has the same area as a radius-8 semicircle: (1/2)π(8^2) = 32π. The shaded area is a radius-4 semicircle with one radius-2 semicircular cap added and an equal radius-2 semicircular cap removed; the radius-2 pieces cancel. Thus the shaded area is just a radius-4 semicircle: (1/2)π(4^2) = 8π. Therefore the shaded fraction is 8π / 32π = 1/4.

method.method_draft: Direct signed-area decomposition. From the image, identify the logo boundary as a large outer upper semicircle spanning the full width, a lower-left bulging semicircle, and a lower-right semicircular cut-out; the shaded lower-left part is further divided by an S-shaped pair of small semicircular arcs. From the text, use that the only radii are 2 cm, 4 cm, and 8 cm, so the full-width outer arc has radius 8, the two medium arcs have radius 4, and the two small divider arcs have radius 2. Use the semicircle area formula A=(1/2)πr^2. The whole logo has area: large radius-8 semicircle + lower-left radius-4 semicircle − lower-right radius-4 semicircle, so the radius-4 terms cancel, leaving the area of a radius-8 semicircle. The shaded region has area equal to a radius-4 semicircle plus one radius-2 semicircular cap minus an equal radius-2 semicircular cap, so the radius-2 terms cancel, leaving the area of a radius-4 semicircle. Therefore the shaded fraction is the ratio of radius-4 to radius-8 semicircle areas, (4^2)/(8^2)=1/4.
